overview.text: The Sharp-tailed Snake is a small, shy, harmless snake of the Pacific coast of the United States and southern British Columbia.

identification.text: A sharp spine at the tip of the tail - the end of the last tail bone. It is harmless and is used to hold slugs still.

size.label: Adults
size.text: About 12 to 18 in (30 to 46 cm) long.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: California, Oregon and Washington, and southern Vancouver Island and nearby parts of British Columbia.

behaviour.text: Secretive; usually found under rocks and logs or burrowing in soft soil, even in towns.

diet.text: Mostly slugs and their eggs; sometimes insects and earthworms.

reproduction.text: Lays 4 to 16 eggs underground in summer; hatchlings are only 3 to 4 in long.

funfacts.text: Its tail ends in a tiny spike that helps it hold slippery slugs.

recognise.text: Sharp little spine on the tail tip.
